organism: Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1; Lactobacillus salivarius ATCC 11741; Thermotoga maritima; E. coli assay host
starting_question: Does a QueG annotation gap mean loss of mature queuosine, or another protein supplying the final reaction?

actual_observations.observation: Authors found inverse QueG/DUF208 distribution, Q-pathway neighborhoods and QueA fusions.
LC-MS detected Q in QueG-lacking L. salivarius grown in rich MRS.
A. baylyi single deletions retained Q; double ΔqueG Δduf208 accumulated oQ and lost Q.
Eight heterologous DUF208 genes restored Q in E. coli ΔqueG, with variable residual oQ.
Purification instability prevented in-vitro validation; limited recombinant-protein spectra did not detect cobalamin.
actual_observations.inspection_location: Cobalamin Seems Not to Be Associated; Conclusions

organism: Escherichia coli K-12; Pseudomonas aeruginosa PhhA system
starting_question: Does rescue of FolA deficiency identify FolM’s ordinary physiological substrate?

actual_observations.observation: Plasmid FolM accelerated growth of ΔthyA ΔfolA on thymidine-supplemented minimal plates; purified FolM reduced dihydrofolate.
No folM deletion was recovered among 47 resolved ΔthyA ΔfolA clones; ΔfolM alone lacked an observed minimal-medium phenotype.
The authors explicitly left normal physiological conditions of FolM function unresolved.
Genome associations suggested monapterin synthesis. Deleting folM blocked PhhA/PhhB-mediated rescue of an E. coli tyrA strain; re-expression restored rescue.
At matched substrate concentration, purified FolM reduced dihydromonapterin faster than dihydrofolate; NADH could not replace NADPH.
FolX deletion removed monapterin without changing folates; P. aeruginosa tyrA/folX combinations corroborated cofactor supply.

annotation_consequence: Dihydromonapterin reductase has physiological support. FolM also has DHFR capacity in a perturbed/overexpressed context; rescue alone cannot assign routine folate-recycling responsibility.
experiment_dependence: Authors used defined genotypes/media, deletion recovery, substrate assays, comparative genomics and pterin measurements.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Experiments and biological results belong to the cited authors. Selection of contrasts and annotation boundaries here is retrospective reconstruction with known outcomes disclosed; no biological experiment was performed.
verification_scope: Complete relevant main texts/methods. P. aeruginosa validation deletes folX, not folM; natural E. coli use of exported monapterin remains unresolved in this study.

starting_question: Can ThyA alone replace ThyX in a bacterium without annotated FolA?

actual_observations.observation: thyX disruption caused thymidine auxotrophy. ThyA alone gave slow/incomplete rescue; ThyA plus FolA restored near-parent growth and more labeled dT synthesis.

annotation_consequence: Same desired dTMP output does not make the alternatives metabolically interchangeable: ThyA replacement imposes folate-recycling demand. No particular native backup reductase was identified.
experiment_dependence: Native gene disruption, controlled complementation and radioactive precursor incorporation.

starting_question: Does recovered growth after DHFR inactivation restore the lost enzyme, or reduce/bypass its demand?

actual_observations.observation: Some D27G trajectories regained supplement independence via G27C; other evolved lineages retained supplement dependence and accumulated thyA/deoB loss mutations.

annotation_consequence: Adaptation can be enzymatic partial restoration or suppressor-driven salvage compensation. The latter did not eliminate all external supplement requirement.

starting_question: Why does loss of the known GAR transformylase not cause purine auxotrophy?

gene_protein: HemJ (ACIAD0878 in A. baylyi) versus HemG/HemY
organism: Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1; Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803
starting_question: Does replacement of a missing PPO family restore all conditions of tetrapyrrole biosynthesis?

actual_observations.observation: A. baylyi hemJ disruption caused heme auxotrophy and porphyrin accumulation; validated PPOs restored growth. Extract PPO activity required combined soluble/membrane fractions.
Synechocystis HemG substitution supported glucose growth but failed photoautotrophic growth with altered intermediates. Purified heme-bound HemJ lacked detectable PPO activity in tested assays.
actual_observations.inspection_location: HemJ not fully replaceable; in-vitro assay subsections

annotation_consequence: HemJ participates in cellular PPO function, with replacement limited by biological context. Isolated catalysis and proposed enzyme coupling were not fully established.
experiment_dependence: Genetics, complementation, extract assays, purification and intermediate analysis.
